findings.finding: The test asserts the README band lies 'inside [min factor, max factor]', i.e. [1.5625, 3.125] using Opus 5.5 factors only. The plan itself says the account-wide upper end is raised by Sonnet traffic priced at the Opus ceilings. Sonnet's ceiling-over-billed factor is not bounded by Opus's 3.125, so that bound is not a true invariant for the account-wide end. The band is also built from a single day's (2026-11-11) mix and labelled as if it were general. The README would then present one day's snapshot as the band, and the test would reject a correct README that reports a Sonnet-heavier upper bound.

scenarios: A Sonnet-heavier day produces a correct settled ratio above 3.125. An operator compares it with the README band, concludes the meter is broken, and a README corrected to reflect it fails the pinning test.
A low-cache-read Opus day settles near 1.6x, below the documented ~1.8x 'lower end', and looks like an anomaly although it is in spec.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the test locates the band endpoints: a fixed anchored phrase or marker in the README (e.g. a single line `Metered/settled band: 1.8x-2.1x`) parsed with an anchored regex, with exactly one match asserted.

findings.finding: The test must extract the band's lower and upper endpoints from README prose, but the plan gives no extraction protocol. The updated README will contain several other 'N.Nx' numbers ('1.56x', '3.1x', 'about 3x', possibly 3.125). A loose regex can grab the wrong pair and pass or fail spuriously (VERIFY-COMMAND taxonomy items 1 and 6: substring false-positive, prose assertion target).
findings.location: Testing section, band lower/upper end assertions
scenarios: The regex matches '1.56x' as the lower end and '3.1x' as the upper end. The assertion passes even though the band text is wrong or missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the README carry one canonical band line, e.g. `Expected metered/settled ratio (5.5 generation): 1.8x–2.1x`. Parse it with `re.findall(r'^Expected metered/settled ratio[^:]*:\s*([0-9.]+)x[–-]([0-9.]+)x', text, re.M)` and assert len == 1 before comparing endpoints.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Write the README band as depending on the traffic mix. Give the limits that follow from the pricing (Opus-only between 1.56x and 3.1x, rising with the cache-read share; higher account-wide as Sonnet and cheaper models are added). Present 1.8x/2.1x as the typical values measured on 2026-11-11/12, not as the ends of the band.
evidence: Plan: 'about 1.8x for the Opus-only mix (lower end) to about 2.1x account-wide'
Measured inputs are a single day's shares (2026-11-11) and ratio (2.04); 2026-11-12 measured 1.94
Test asserts 'the band inside [min factor, max factor]' — i.e., the plan already knows the real limits are 1.5625x and 3.125x for Opus
README line 54-56: cheapest models are 'two orders of magnitude below the ceiling'
findings.finding: The new band (about 1.8x to about 2.1x) comes from one or two settled days, but the plan labels its ends as if they were limits ('lower end' is the Opus-only mix, 'upper end' is account-wide). The ratio depends on the traffic mix. For Opus alone it can fall toward 1.5625x on a day with a smaller cache-read share, and it can rise toward 3.125x as the cache-read share grows. Account-wide it goes above 2.1x on any day with more Sonnet or small-model traffic: the measured 2.04 leaves only 0.06 of margin, and the README already says the cheapest models are two orders of magnitude below the ceiling. So ordinary day-to-day changes in the mix will put the metered estimate outside the documented band again, and this same bug will be reported again. The plan's own test admits the wider range: it only checks that the band sits inside [1.5625, 3.125].
findings.location: ## Approach — 'Replace the 1.1-1.9x band with the measured band for the 5.5 generation, labelled by what each end is'
scenarios: A day with more Sonnet traffic or batch/embedding jobs gives an account-wide ratio of about 2.3x on a settled day. An operator compares it with the README, sees it outside the band, and files the same bug again.
A day with a smaller Opus cache-read share gives about 1.65x, which falls below the documented 'lower end'.
findings.suggested_fix: In the README, state that the metered/settled ratio for Opus 5.5 lies between about 1.56x (no cache reads) and about 3.1x (all cache reads), that it typically measures about 1.8x for the current Opus mix and about 2.0-2.1x account-wide (settled 2026-11-11/12), and that more Sonnet or smaller-model traffic pushes it higher. Change the test to check the typical values against the measured constants and to check that the stated limits equal min/max of the factors.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Approach section, give a positive reason for README-only. State whether re-deriving CEILING over the current trailing 60-day window (the procedure in handler.py) would change any value, and if it would not, why (e.g. 4.x Opus still billed, so lowering the ceilings would break the upper bound). Also state explicitly that tripping at about half the configured cap, which denied production roles on 2026-11-12, is accepted.
evidence: Plan: 'The ceilings still match their written definition; the documented band is stale.'
handler.py:101-109: 'Each value is 1.25x the highest per-token rate this account was billed for that direction over the trailing 60 days of Cost Explorer, derived 2026-09-25 ... Re-derive with: ...'
Plan Observation: deny attached 'to every capped role, including rebar-gerrit-instance-role'
AC: 'Either the ceiling table is corrected or the README band is updated with the measured reason'
findings.finding: The plan does not say why it keeps the 4.x-derived ceilings rather than re-deriving CEILING with the procedure handler.py itself documents ('1.25x the highest per-token rate ... over the trailing 60 days', derived 2026-09-25, with re-derive instructions). Re-deriving is a data-only change inside the existing mechanism, not the new mechanism the plan rules out. The plan's only reason, 'The ceilings still match their written definition', is unclear. The definition is a dated snapshot, so it matches trivially. The plan does not say whether a re-derivation over the current 60-day window would give the same values (because 4.x models are still billed there) or lower ones. The plan also never says it accepts the consequence its own Observation records: the metered arm now trips at about half the configured cap (settled ratio about 1.94), and that denied bedrock:InvokeModel to production roles such as rebar-gerrit-instance-role. That is far more than the 1.25x headroom the handler describes as deliberate.
scenarios: 4.x models dropped out of the 60-day window. Re-deriving would bring the headroom back to about 1.25x, and README-only leaves production denied at about 50% of the configured cap every heavy day.

4.x models are still billed in the window. Re-deriving would change nothing, and the plan should say so to show README-only is the only safe choice (lowering the ceilings would let the metered arm fire late).
